chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi Najran, from 'Asim, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gave judgment concerning four persons who were partners in a camel. One of them hobbled it, then the camel moved off and meddled with its hobble, then fell down and was broken. So his partners said to the one who had hobbled it, 'Compensate us for our camel.'
He said: So he judged between them that they should compensate him for his share, because he had secured his share more firmly, and their share was lost along with his share.

key_terms.أَوْثَقَ: he secured more firmly or took stronger precaution
key_terms.بَعِيرٍ: a camel as jointly owned property
key_terms.حَظَّهُ: his allotted share in the jointly owned asset
key_terms.عَقَلَهُ: he hobbled it or tied it in restraint
key_terms.فَتَرَدَّى: it fell down from a height or into a harmful fall
key_terms.فَٱنْكَسَرَ: it was broken or fatally damaged

ai.seo_question: In Shia fiqh, who bears liability when jointly owned property is lost after one partner took proper precaution?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام regarding shared property and liability among partners. It establishes that when one partner took proper precaution concerning the jointly owned camel, he was not held liable for the loss of the others' shares; rather, they were required to compensate him for his own share.
